name: Basel and the Alsace: Basel, Strasbourg, Colmar, wine road

cities.base: Altstadt Grossbasel round Marktplatz and Barfusserplatz: most sights are a 5 to 15 minute walk, and Old Town doubles run about 200 to 400 dollars.
cities.name: Basel

cities.base: The Grande Ile between the cathedral and Petite France, which puts the winstubs, the Palais Rohan museums and the Ponts Couverts all on foot.
cities.name: Strasbourg

cities.base: The old town between Petite Venise and Unterlinden: everything on the Colmar list is within 1.5 km, and Eguisheim and Riquewihr are 7 and 11 km out.
cities.name: Colmar

places.name: Schlusselzunft (Zunftstube)
places.note: The guild-house dining room on Freie Strasse: the Business Lunch is CHF 55 for two courses or CHF 69 for three, amuse-bouche included, and the lunch days are not stated, so check. Shut Sundays and public holidays, to 23:00 Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Brasserie Zum Braunen Mutz
places.note: The beer-hall brasserie on Barfusserplatz. Order the Basler Geschnetzeltes with Spatzli at CHF 27.50, or the half-metre cordon bleu at CHF 69 to share; open daily, to 23:30 Friday and Saturday and 22:30 Sunday, and busy at lunch.

places.name: Torstubli
places.note: Evenings from 16:00, with a game menu dated 15 October 2026: venison cheeks CHF 39, wild boar saltimbocca CHF 44, starters CHF 18.50 to 24.50. Shut Sunday and Monday, to 23:30 on Saturday.

places.name: Restaurant Lowenzorn
places.note: Swiss classics and offal alongside chef Anwar's Pakistani-influenced dishes: cheese fondue CHF 33.50, calf liver and Rosti CHF 34. Weekdays break 14:00 to 16:30, no Saturday lunch, Sunday 14:00 to 22:00, Friday to midnight.

places.name: Walliser Kanne
places.note: Fondue, raclette and schnitzel off the 2026 menu: cheese fondue is CHF 42 a head, veal Wiener schnitzel CHF 48, pork CHF 40. Shut Sundays, open to midnight the rest of the week.

places.name: Basel Munster
places.note: Rebuilt by Johannes Gmund after the 1356 earthquake, towers finished 1429 and 1500. See the 15th-century cloisters and Anne of Habsburg's tomb, then climb 242 steps for the Rhine. Winter weekday hours shown, summer 10:00 to 17:00; fees not stated, check the price.

places.name: Kunstmuseum Basel
places.note: The city collection, 15th to 21st century, CHF 25 or CHF 30 with the special show. Free Tuesday, Thursday and Friday 17:00 to 18:00, Wednesday 17:00 to 20:00 and first Sundays; shut Mondays, and the Gegenwart wing is closed to 27 Nov 2026.

places.name: Historisches Museum Basel, Barfusserkirche
places.note: A former Franciscan church holding the Dance of Death fresco, cathedral treasures and rebuilt Gothic rooms. One ticket covers three houses for 7 days, but the official site shows no fare, so check the price. Shut Mondays; English by QR code.

places.name: Pharmacy Museum of the University of Basel
places.note: Alchemy, faience and 16th to 19th-century pharmacy objects in a 15th-century house. CHF 10 with a free audioguide, and the ticket also gets you into the Anatomical Museum the same or next opening day; shut Mondays and most public holidays.

places.name: Museum der Kulturen Basel
places.note: The ethnographic collection on Munsterplatz, CHF 16. Free on the first Sunday of the month and in the last opening hour Tuesday to Saturday, and first Wednesdays it stays open to 20:00. Shut Mondays.

places.name: Antikenmuseum Basel und Sammlung Ludwig
places.note: Greek, Etruscan and Roman antiquities, CHF 18. Thursday and Friday it runs to 22:00 and is free from 17:00, though the vase rooms close then; weekends 10:00 to 16:00, shut Mondays. The Skulpturhalle next door is free.

places.name: Basler Papiermuhle
places.note: The paper, writing and printing museum in a working medieval mill on the St. Alban canal, where you can make your own sheet. Ticket and workshop prices were not on the pages read, so check the price; Saturday from 13:00, shut Mondays.

places.name: Museum Tinguely
places.note: Jean Tinguely's kinetic machines, a tram ride out rather than a walk from the Old Town. The official price page would not load and a third party quotes 19.42 euros, so check the price; Thursday to 21:00, shut Mondays.

places.name: Rathaus (Town Hall)
places.note: The red sandstone town hall on Marktplatz, over 500 years old, with frescoes and a wooden staircase; the cantonal parliament still sits here. Free, weekdays with a 12:00 to 12:30 break, shut weekends.

places.name: University of Basel Botanical Garden
places.note: The university's garden at Spalengraben 8, free and open daily 08:00 to 18:00. A quiet 45 minutes a few streets from the Pharmacy Museum.

places.name: Tinguely Fountain (Fasnachtsbrunnen)
places.note: Tinguely's machine fountain, free and open at any hour, a couple of minutes from Barfusserplatz. Stop on the way to the Kunstmuseum.

places.name: Markthalle Basel
places.note: The covered market hall; no entry fee is stated and stall prices were not checked, so check the price. Open daily from 09:00, to 22:00 Sunday and Monday, midnight Tuesday to Thursday and 02:00 Friday and Saturday.

places.name: Au Pont Corbeau
places.note: Family winstub by the Musee Alsacien, Bib Gourmand per Le Bonbon; the formule is about 17 euros, a la carte 25 to 50. Shut Saturdays, Sunday dinner from 19:00, and open daily during the Christmas market. Michelin gives 22:00 closing, Gault&Millau 23:30.

places.name: La Vieille Enseigne
places.note: On Michelin's winstub best-of. Order the seven-meat choucroute at 28 euros, with the onion tart at 9 to start; there is no fixed adult menu. Lunch 12:00 to 14:00, dinner 19:00 to 22:00, shut Tuesdays.

places.name: Winstub Le Clou
places.note: Winstub cooking two streets from the cathedral: grandmother's pot-au-feu at 21.90 euros, veal kidneys at 23.10, onion tart at 11.50. Lunch 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner 19:00 to 23:30, every day.

places.name: Chez Yvonne (S'Burjerstuewel)
places.note: The best-known winstub in town and on every list, so book ahead. Smoked sausage with sauerkraut is 20.50 euros, veal head 25.90; lunch 12:00 to 14:00 and dinner 19:00 to 23:30, every day.

places.name: Cathedrale Notre-Dame de Strasbourg
places.note: Free nave, shut to visits 11:15 to 12:45. Schwilgue's 1838 to 1842 astronomical clock performs at 12:30 after a 12:00 film, 4 euros, sold on the day; queue by 11:00, and some Christmas-market days have no show. Sunday 14:00 to 17:15; platform climb, check the price.

places.name: Musee de l'Oeuvre Notre-Dame
places.note: The cathedral's own sculpture and stained glass in the cathedral workshop buildings, 9 euros, less with a platform ticket. Tuesday to Friday it breaks 13:00 to 14:00; shut Mondays.

places.name: Musee historique de la Ville de Strasbourg
places.note: The city history museum, 9 euros or 5 reduced, a few minutes south of the cathedral. Tuesday to Friday it breaks 13:00 to 14:00; shut Mondays.

places.name: Palais Rohan
places.note: The palace holding the Beaux-Arts, Decorative Arts and Archaeology museums and the Galerie Heitz. Each is 9 euros, or 20 for the one-day Palais Rohan pass; weekdays break 13:00 to 14:00, shut Tuesdays.

places.name: Musee des Beaux-Arts de Strasbourg
places.note: The fine-art collection on the upper floors of Palais Rohan, 9 euros or part of the 20-euro one-day Rohan pass. Weekdays break 13:00 to 14:00, weekends run straight through; shut Tuesdays.

places.name: Musee d'Art moderne et contemporain (MAMCS)
places.note: Modern and contemporary art at place Hans-Jean-Arp, 9 euros. Tuesday to Friday it breaks 13:00 to 14:00, shut Mondays; the Barrage Vauban is a 2-minute walk, so do both together.

places.name: Barrage Vauban
places.note: Vauban's dam across the river, free and open 07:15 to 21:00 every day, a couple of minutes from both MAMCS and the Ponts Couverts. Walk it between the two.

places.name: Ponts Couverts
places.note: The bridges and towers at the west end of Petite France, free to cross and listed 09:00 to 19:00. On every list, so come in the morning before the quays fill.

places.name: Eglise Saint-Pierre-le-Jeune
places.note: A church about 500 m north-west of the cathedral, listed 10:00 to 18:00 every day; any entry charge was not confirmed, so check the price. A quiet half hour away from the cathedral crowds.

places.name: Parc de l'Orangerie
places.note: The city's big park, free and open 07:00 to 20:00, about 2 km north-east of the cathedral. Take the tram out and give it a slow hour in the afternoon.

places.name: Cave Historique des Hospices de Strasbourg
places.note: Wine has been made in this hospital cellar for over 600 years, kept going since 1997 by about 30 Alsace estates. Reviewers say entry is free but the site lists no prices, so check the price. Weekdays break 12:00 to 13:30, Saturday 09:00 to 12:30, shut Sundays.

places.name: Wistub Brenner
places.note: Choucroute, braised pork shank and Munster salad in Petite Venise: starter and main 40.90 euros, three courses 48.90. Kitchen 12:00 to 14:00 and 19:00 to 22:00, afternoon menu to 15:45; book for the Christmas market, tables up to 12.

places.name: Restaurant Quai 21
places.note: Google 4.7, and the way in is the three-course Quai a Midi at 31 euros, Tuesday to Friday lunch, last order 13:30; the Quai 21 menu is 65. Dinner last order 20:30. Shut Sunday and Monday, but open Sundays during the Christmas markets.

places.name: Matoine Bistrot
places.note: Google 4.8 in a small room, so book. The menu du jour was 24 euros for two courses or 28 for three in late October 2026, dinner 45 or 51. Shut weekends and, per its site, Wednesday evening; Wanderlog shows other days, so confirm.

places.name: La Fleur de Sel
places.note: Tartes flambees on the Petite Venise quay, 13 euros plain up to 15.50 for the house Fleur de Sel. Lunch from 12:00; Wanderlog shows Thursday to Saturday to 17:00, so confirm. Shut Tuesday and Wednesday.

places.name: Musee des Vins d'Alsace
places.note: An audio tour of Alsace wine that ends in a three-wine tasting, 15 euros, at 12 place de la Cathedrale through the chocolate museum's door. Sessions run daily between 10:00 and 16:30; book a day ahead.

places.name: Domaine Joseph Gruss
places.note: A wine estate at 25 Grand-Rue in Eguisheim: Monday to Saturday 10:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 18:00, Sunday 10:00 to 12:00. One reviewer mentions glasses at about a euro, unconfirmed, so check the price.

places.name: Musee Unterlinden
places.note: Home of the Issenheim Altarpiece. Book on the museum's Vivaticket page and go at 09:00; the price page would not load, so check the price. Last entry 17:30, shut Tuesdays and on 1 Jan, 1 May, 1 Nov and 25 Dec.

places.name: La Petite Venise
places.note: The canal quarter along the quai de la Poissonnerie, free at any hour; Brenner, Quai 21 and La Fleur de Sel are all on it. Walk it early in the morning or after dark.

places.name: Collegiale Saint-Martin
places.note: The big church on place de la Cathedrale, free with a donation box, reviewers say. Monday to Saturday 08:00 to 18:45, Sunday 10:00 to 19:00; the wine museum tasting is on the same square.

places.name: Maison Pfister
places.note: One of Colmar's historic houses at 11 rue des Marchands, seen free from the street; Wanderlog lists 10:00 to 19:00. It sits a minute from both Saint-Martin and the Bartholdi museum.

places.name: Eglise des Dominicains
places.note: Hours shift by day: Tuesday, Thursday and Sunday 10:00 to 13:00 and 15:00 to 18:00, Wednesday from 15:00, Friday and Saturday 10:00 to 18:00, shut Mondays. One reviewer says 2 euros, unconfirmed, so check the price.

places.name: Musee Bartholdi
places.note: The museum of Auguste Bartholdi, the Colmar-born sculptor of the Statue of Liberty, at 30 rue des Marchands. Tuesday to Sunday 10:00 to 12:00 and 14:00 to 18:00, shut Mondays; no fare found, so check the price.

places.name: Musee du Jouet
places.note: The toy museum at 40 rue Vauban, about 7 dollars by the official fare Wanderlog quotes, not confirmed on the museum's own site. 10:00 to 17:00 and shut Tuesdays, but 10:00 to 18:00 every day from 17 to 31 Oct 2026.

places.name: Maison des Tetes
places.note: The house front at 19 rue des Tetes, free to look at from the street; interior hours and prices were not found. Two minutes from Unterlinden, so take it in on the way.

places.name: Quartier des Tanneurs
places.note: The old tanners' quarter next to the covered market, free to wander. Half an hour; pair it with the market in the morning.

places.name: Marche Couvert Colmar
places.note: The covered market at 13 rue des Ecoles; no entry fee is stated and stall prices were not checked. Tuesday to Thursday 08:00 to 18:00, Friday to 19:00, Saturday to 17:00, Sunday 10:00 to 14:00, shut Mondays.

places.name: Eguisheim
places.note: The wine village where Pope Leo IX was born on 21 June 1002, with the 11th-century castle of the Dukes of Alsace. Walk the Sentier viticole through the vines, see the free stork park, and taste at Domaine Joseph Gruss.

places.name: Riquewihr
places.note: A wine village inside medieval ramparts, little changed since the 16th century. The streets are free; inside the walls are a castle museum and a WWII Alsace museum. On every list, so go early.

places.name: Chateau du Haut-Koenigsbourg
places.note: Rebuilt 1900 to 1908 by Bodo Ebhardt for Kaiser Wilhelm II; the keep is thought 14 m too tall. 12 euros self-guided, 16 audio, no booking needed; 09:30 to 18:00 to 31 Oct, last entry an hour before, check later dates. No closing day listed.

places.name: Koifhus (Ancienne Douane)
places.note: The old customs house, built 1480 in Gothic and Renaissance style, listed since 1930 and the birthplace of General Jean Rapp. Free to see from the square; it holds a restaurant and fairs, and no visiting hours were found, so check the price for any event.

destination.name: Basel and the Alsace: Basel, Strasbourg, Colmar, wine road
destination.pitch: Three beds about an hour apart by train: Basel for the Munster and its museums, Strasbourg for the cathedral clock and the winstubs, Colmar for the Issenheim Altarpiece and the wine villages. Two nights in each is the shape.
destination.caveat: Basel is the dear one: a set lunch is 67 dollars and museums 19 to 30. Nearly every Basel and Strasbourg museum shuts Monday, Unterlinden Tuesday. Strasbourg's Christmas market opens 27 Nov 2026; those weekends are shoulder to shoulder and December rooms run 361 to 399 dollars. Put together for you just now from a live search, so check anything you're pinning the trip on.

because.city: Three old towns you walk: Basel's Marktplatz and Munsterhugel, Strasbourg's Grande Ile from the cathedral to the Ponts Couverts, and Colmar's Petite Venise and tanners' quarter.
because.food: Seven-meat choucroute at La Vieille Enseigne, pot-au-feu at Le Clou, tartes flambees at La Fleur de Sel, a 31-euro lunch menu at Quai 21, fondue at Walliser Kanne and game in season at Torstubli.
because.culture: The Issenheim Altarpiece at Unterlinden, Schwilgue's astronomical clock in Strasbourg cathedral, the Kunstmuseum's 15th to 21st-century collection, Basel Munster rebuilt after 1356, and the Palais Rohan museums on one 20-euro pass.
because.exploration: Eguisheim, where Leo IX was born in 1002, and walled Riquewihr on the wine road, Basel's working paper mill on the St. Alban canal, and a wine cellar under Strasbourg's hospital in use for over 600 years.
